Background & Challenge

USER PROBLEM
Exchange applicants had to piece together school requirements, acceptance stories, and grade benchmarks from scattered sheets and rumors.
BUSINESS GOAL & CONSTRAINTS
Make application prep easier to manage, increase verified mentor matching, and lower informational page bounce rates below 15%.
CORE DESIGN HYPOTHESIS
“A 9-step application wizard would make the process feel manageable and reduce form drop-off by showing only one decision at a time.”

"We turned an uncertain exchange application process into a clearer path powered by data, reviews, and mentor support."

Research & Insights

We interviewed and surveyed 50+ applicants and recent exchange students to find where preparation became confusing or stressful.

Scattered School Data

Users spent 40+ hours searching for requirements across sheets, blogs, and school pages. A filterable database could cut search time and help users start faster.

Acceptance Anxiety

Users delayed decisions because they could not judge their chances. Real-time applicant specs and mock competition rates could make the next step feel safer.

Design Strategy

Research pointed to three priorities: clearer data, less decision pressure, and stronger trust. We mapped each priority to a specific user type.

Opportunity

Data Transparency

Bring school data into one interface so users can compare options quickly.

Opportunity

Anxiety Relief

Use real-time data and peer signals to help users judge their chances.

Strategy

Guided Discovery

For early-stage users, show trending schools and beginner guides first.

Strategy

Mock Application

For preparing users, show live competition rates and applicant specs.

Strategy

Verified Mentoring

For users with specific questions, connect them to verified alumni.

The Solution

The final design prioritized clarity, data visualization, and community engagement.

04Collaboration & Influence

Role-Based UI & Developer Alignment

How we balanced different user needs with engineering scope to launch on time.

The Conflict

Two Roles, One Deadline

Mentors needed schedule management. Mentees needed search and Q&A. Their goals were different, but the team had one 5-month launch window.

Two fully separate dashboards would double development time and put the launch at risk.

The Rationale

Why One Page Wasn't Enough

Merging both roles into one page would make the flow crowded and confusing.

It would also make future maintenance harder. We needed role clarity without rebuilding everything twice.

The Resolution

One Shell, Two Experiences

I proposed one shared framework: the same navigation and layout, with role-specific content inside.

This saved 40% of development time while keeping each role's experience clean.

Key Takeaway

“Good design aligns user needs with team constraints, then turns both into a clear system.”

Outcome & Impact

Results & Learnings

Based on GA4 Data: Jan 1, 2025 - Dec 16, 2025
2.0kActive Users
2.0kNew Users
83kTotal Events
2m 56sAvg. Session Time

Qualitative Feedback

“This finally makes the exchange application predictable.”

“I don't need to ask seniors every semester anymore.”

Traffic & Acquisition

Strong Seasonality

Traffic peaks in Jan-Feb and Sep-Oct, matching university application seasons. The product works best as a trusted seasonal problem-solving tool.

Community-Driven Growth

Referrals came from university communities and messengers such as Everytime and Kakao. Word-of-mouth was strong among exchange applicants.

Analysis & Next Steps

High Churn on First Screen

Inner pages performed well, including School List at 5.6% churn. The Main Page had 21.4% churn, showing that the first CTA needed to be clearer.

PageViews / Churn
Main Page24k / 21.4%
Beginner's Guide6.3k / 12.5%
School List3.9k / 5.6%

Next Strategies

1. Main UX Simplification

Use one clear first-screen CTA that leads users to a core action within 60 seconds.

2. Retention Experiments

Add “Save School” and “D-3 Deadline Alerts” to support repeat visits and track 7/30-day retention.

3. Data Integrity

Define conversion events such as School Search and Signup, then apply UTM tags to community channels.
